claims.label: Theorem 1
claims.statement_original:
If $\kappa_U$ and $\kappa_\Theta$ are characteristic, then so is tensor product kernel $\kappa_U\otimes\kappa_\Theta$; that is, the mapping
\[
\mathcal M(\Omega_{U,\Theta},\mathcal F_{U,\Theta})\to\mathcal H_U\otimes\mathcal H_\Theta,\qquad P_{U,\Theta}\mapsto\int_{\Omega_{U,\Theta}}\kappa_U(\cdot,U)\otimes\kappa_\Theta(\cdot,\Theta)\,dP_{U,\Theta}
\]
is injective.

claims.label: Theorem 2
claims.statement_original:
If the statistical functional $F\mapsto\Sigma_{U\Theta}(F)$ is Frechet differentiable at $F_0$ with respect to the uniform metric in $\mathcal F$ and conditions in (5.11) are satisfied, then
\[
\sqrt n(\breve\Sigma_{U\Theta}-\Sigma_{U\Theta})\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}N(0,\Gamma),
\]
where $\Gamma:\mathcal H_U\otimes\mathcal H_\Theta\to\mathcal H_U\otimes\mathcal H_\Theta$ is the operator
\[
\Gamma=E[\Sigma_{U\Theta}^\star(X)\otimes\Sigma_{U\Theta}^\star(X)],
\]
and $\Sigma_{U\Theta}^\star(z)$ is given by (5.10).

claims.label: Theorem 3
claims.statement_original:
Suppose
1. $\Gamma$ has spectral decomposition $\sum_{j=1}^\infty\lambda_j(v_j\otimes v_j)$, where $v_1,v_2,\ldots$ is an orthonormal basis in $\mathcal H_U\otimes\mathcal H_\Theta$;
2. $\Sigma_1$ is a fixed linear operator in $\mathcal H_U\otimes\mathcal H_\Theta$ with expansion $\sum_{j=1}^\infty\sigma_jv_j$ and $\|\Sigma_1\|_{\mathrm{HS}}=c>0$.
Then, under the local alternative hypothesis $H_1^{(n)}:\Sigma_{U\Theta}=n^{-1/2}\Sigma_1$, we have
\[
n\|\breve\Sigma_{U\Theta}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\sum_{j=1}^\infty\lambda_j\widetilde Z_j^2
\]
where $\widetilde Z_j$ are independent $N(\sigma_j/\sqrt{\lambda_j},1)$ random variables.

claims.label: Theorem 4
claims.statement_original:
Suppose that $\mu$ and $\Sigma$ are known and $\breve\Sigma_{U\Theta}$ is defined as (7.1). Furthermore, suppose the kernels $\kappa_U$ and $\kappa_\Theta$ are bounded: $0\le\kappa_U(u,u')\le M_U$ and $0\le\kappa_\Theta(\theta,\theta')\le M_\Theta$ for all $u,u',\theta,\theta'$. Then,
\[
P\left(\left|\|\breve\Sigma_{U\Theta}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}-\|\Sigma_{U\Theta}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\right|\ge t+4(M_UM_\Theta/n)^{1/2}\right)\le\exp\left(-\frac{t^2n}{10M_UM_\Theta}\right).
\]
(7.2)

claims.label: Theorem 5
claims.statement_original:
Suppose $X$ satisfies Assumption 2, and $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are i.i.d samples of $X$. Further suppose $\Sigma$ satisfies Assumption 1, the density of $W$ satisfies Assumption 3, and the kernel functions $\kappa_U$ and $\kappa_\Theta$ satisfy Assumption 4. Then, for any $\epsilon>0$, we have
\[
P\left(\left|\|\breve\Sigma_{U\Theta}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}-\|\Sigma_{U\Theta}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\right|\ge[c_7+2c_8/(\epsilon d)]\times[f_3(n,d,u)f_2(n,d,u)+c_5f_1(n,d,u)]+f_4(n,u)\right)\le n(c_6\epsilon)^d+7e^{-u},
\]
where $f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4$ are as defined in (7.6), and $c_1,\ldots,c_{10}$ are some positive absolute constants.

claims.label: Theorem 6
claims.statement_original:
Suppose all conditions in Theorem 5 are satisfied. If $\log n\prec d\prec n^{1/4}$, then
\[
\|\breve\Sigma_{U\Theta}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\xrightarrow{P}\|\Sigma_{U\Theta}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}.
\]

members.statement_original:
Let $\mathcal B$ be the collection of linear operators $\{f\otimes g:f\in\mathcal H_U,g\in\mathcal H_\Theta\}$. Thus, each member of $\mathcal B$ is a linear operator mapping from $\mathcal H_\Theta$ to $\mathcal H_U$ such that, for any $h\in\mathcal H_\Theta$, $(f\otimes g)(h)=f\langle g,h\rangle_{\mathcal H_\Theta}$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the linear span of $\mathcal B$, consisting of finite linear combinations of members of $\mathcal B$ with real coefficients. Define in $\mathcal S$ the inner product
\[
\langle\alpha_1(f_1\otimes g_1)+\cdots+\alpha_r(f_r\otimes g_r),\widetilde\alpha_1(\widetilde f_1\otimes\widetilde g_1)+\cdots+\widetilde\alpha_r(\widetilde f_s\otimes\widetilde g_s)\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^r\sum_{j=1}^s\alpha_i\widetilde\alpha_j\langle f_i,\widetilde f_j\rangle_{\mathcal H_U}\langle g_i,\widetilde g_j\rangle_{\mathcal H_\Theta}.
\]
Endowed with this inner product, $\mathcal S$ is an inner product space; its completion as a Hilbert space is the tensor product space $\mathcal H_U\otimes\mathcal H_\Theta$.

\arctan(y/x)-\pi,&x<0,y<0,\\
\pi/2,&x=0,y>0,\\
-\pi/2,&x=0,y<0.
\end{cases}
\]

members.statement_original:
In the following, we use $S_j$ to denote the Euclidean norm of the vector $(v_j,\ldots,v_d)^\top$.
The following function from $\Omega_\Theta$ to $S^{d-1}$
\[
v_1=\sin\theta_1,\quad v_2=\cos\theta_1\sin\theta_2,\quad\ldots,\quad v_{d-1}=\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2\cdots\cos\theta_{d-2}\sin\theta_{d-1},\quad v_d=\cos\theta_1\cos\theta_2\cdots\cos\theta_{d-2}\cos\theta_{d-1}.
\]
(2.6)
is bijective with inverse
\[
\theta_j=\begin{cases}\operatorname{Arctan}(S_{j+1},v_j),&j=1,\ldots,d-2,\\\operatorname{Arctan}(v_d,v_{d-1}),&j=d-1.\end{cases}
\]
(2.7)
We will denote the first function (2.6) as $v=\rho(\theta)$ and the second function (2.7) as $\theta=g(v)$. Then $x=uv=u\rho(\theta)\equiv\tau(u,\theta)$.
